kind: A diagnostic of trained weights, chosen before anything is measured: how loud the loudest channels of a stream are where a Transformer's norms and a stack's pools hear it.
why: energy_pool.json: a pool dividing by the root mean square costs the Transformer only 0.0020 against its LayerNorm, where the stack's pool, dividing by the mean absolute activity, cost it 0.0691; but the spiking energy pool, hearing sqrt(d * sum x^2) in place of sum |x|, is 0.0040 behind at full size and fails on the bed. A stream divided by its mean absolute activity keeps an energy that grows with the ratio of its root mean square to its mean absolute value, so where that ratio jumps from token to token the next layer's input jumps with it. The guess: a Transformer's stream is signed and dense with a few channels far louder than the rest on some tokens, so the ratio jumps through loudness, while the stack's counts are whole and capped, so no channel can be far louder, and its ratio moves, if at all, with the share of channels that fire, which an energy pool then punishes.
measure: experiments/stream_loudness.py (this commit, tests/test_stream_loudness.py) on the averaged weights, on the laptop's CPU. For every token of the stream that a norm or a pool hears, with its d channels x, L1 = sum |x|, Q = sum x^2 and k active channels: the ratio sqrt(d Q) / L1, the loudness sqrt(k Q) / L1 (1 when the active channels are equally loud) and the share k / d, so that ratio = loudness * sqrt(d / k); silent tokens counted and left out; the 10th, 50th, 90th and 99th percentiles over tokens of each, for every place. Transformers fs-tf3 (LayerNorm) and fs-tf3-pool (the stack's pool): the first 65,536 validation bytes in windows of 512, the input of every norm. Stacks fs-loop6-lift (pools of summed activity) and fs-loop6-lift-en (energy pools): the first 16,384 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams of 1,024 from an empty state, in pieces of 256, the stream that every pool hears (reads, cells, output; a looped stack's tied pools are one place).
reading: (1) The Transformer's stream has loud tokens if at more than half of fs-tf3's norms the ratio's 99th percentile is at least 1.5 times its median. (2) The stack's streams have no loud channels if at every pool of fs-loop6-lift the loudness's 99th percentile is within 1.2 times its median. If (1) and (2) hold, what the stack's pool costs a Transformer is the Transformer's own: the stack's pools keep hearing summed activity and the layout walk moves to its next part. If (1) holds and (2) fails, the stack has loud channels at the pools where (2) fails, and a pool hearing the energy of the active channels only, sqrt(k Q), which leaves sparse patterns alone, is the next candidate, pre-registered then. If (1) fails, loud tokens are not what the pool costs a Transformer, and the measures are reported as found. fs-tf3-pool and fs-loop6-lift-en are reported beside, for what each kind of division does to the loudness.
seen_before_recording: energy_pool.json with its three results; no loudness, ratio or share of active channels has been computed on any trained model.

result.measures: stream_loudness_measures.json (every place's quantiles of ratio, loudness and share of active channels)

summary.fs-tf3 (LayerNorm): ratio median 1.243 to 1.256 at the 23 norms, 99th percentile 1.024 to 1.053 times the median; every channel active
summary.fs-tf3-pool (pool): ratio median 1.198 to 1.326 in the blocks and 1.530 at the last norm, 99th percentile 1.034 to 1.175 times the median; every channel active
summary.fs-loop6-lift (pools of summed activity): ratio median 1.218 to 1.345, rising toward the top and the output; loudness 99th percentile 1.020 to 1.081 times the median at the 23 pools; 96% to 99% of channels active (the 10th percentile never below 0.961)
summary.fs-loop6-lift-en (energy pools): ratio median 1.250 to 1.255 at every pool, 99th percentile 1.016 to 1.031 times the median; 96% to 99% of channels active

result.reading: (1) fails: at none of fs-tf3's 23 norms does the ratio's 99th percentile reach 1.5 times its median (at most 1.053), so the Transformer's stream has no loud tokens and loud tokens are not what the pool costs a Transformer. (2) holds: at every pool of fs-loop6-lift the loudness's 99th percentile is within 1.2 times its median (at most 1.081). Reported as found: both streams are dense and close to Gaussian in their magnitudes, the ratio near sqrt(pi/2) = 1.2533, and it barely moves from token to token, so in both trained models a division by the mean absolute activity is, within a few percent, a division by the root mean square times a constant that the gains absorb. What the pool costs the Transformer (0.069, with 97% of it recovered by the root mean square) is therefore not in what the trained division computes; it lies in how the division trains, through its gradient (that of the mean absolute activity is the stream's sign pattern, that of the root mean square the stream itself) or in early updates before the stream settles, neither of which this measure sees. Beside it: a pool of summed activity lets the upper levels' streams grow heavier-tailed in both models (the ratio up to 1.345 at the stack's output and 1.530 at the Transformer's last norm), where division by energy holds every place at 1.25.
